label: thm:n0
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:n0}
We set $X'=M_H(r_0 e^{-\frac{q}{p}H})$ and assume that there is a universal family
${\mathcal E}$.
Let $v=(r,dH,a)$ be a Mukai vector such that
\begin{equation*}
r \geq 0, \; pd-rq>0,-\langle e^{\frac{q}{p}H}, v \rangle \geq 0,\;
\langle v^2 \rangle \geq -2.
\end{equation*}
Assume that $n \geq (2r+p)p$.
Then
                  
            
$D_{X'} \circ \Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}}(E) \in {\mathcal M}_{H'}(v')$
for a general $E \in {\mathcal M}_H(v) \setminus Z$, where 
$D_{X'}:{\bf D}(X') \to {\bf D}(X')$ is the taking dual functor (see \eqref{eq:dualize}), 
$v'=\Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}}(v)$ and $Z$ is a closed substack of ${\mathcal M}_H(v)$. 
           
                         
                                   
                              
                  
      
                                                   
      
                      
                             
                
                
Moreover
$\dim Z \leq \dim {\mathcal M}_H(v)-2$ if $r>0$.

title: Remark
head: environment

label: rem:disprepant
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:disprepant}
For an abelian surface, walls for Bridgeland stability corresponds to walls for birational geometry. 
On the other hand, for a K3 surface
we have discrepancy 
between walls for Bridgeland stability and walls for birational geometry. 
Indeed totally semistable walls by spherical objects do not affect birational geometry of the moduli space
(cf. sebsection \ref{subsect:n=1}).
head: environment

title: Problem
body_md:
Assume that $\Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}}$ induces a birational map
of the moduli of stable sheaves.
Study the properties of ${\mathcal E}$.

For example, does ${\mathcal E}$ parameterize stable sheaves?
head: environment

label: defn:B-stable
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{defn:B-stable}
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)]
A $\sigma$-semi-stable object $E$ of phase $\phi$ is
an object of  ${\mathcal P}_\sigma(\phi)$.
If $E$ is a simple object of ${\mathcal P}_\sigma(\phi)$, then
$E$ is $\sigma$-stable. 
\item[(2)]
For $v \in H^*(X,{\mathbb Z})_{\operatorname{alg}}$,
we denote the moduli stack of $\sigma$-semi-stable objects $E$ with 
$v(E)=v$ by ${\mathcal M}_\sigma(v)$,
where we usually choose 
$\phi:=\mathrm{Im}(\log Z_\sigma(v))/\pi \in (-1,1]$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: defn:W
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{defn:W}
We fix a Mukai vector $v=(r,dH,a)$.
For a Mukai vector $v_1=(r_1,d_1 H,a_1)$ with $v_1 \not \in {\mathbb Q}v$,
let $W_{v_1}$ be a closed subset of ${\mathbb H}$ such that
$$
W_{v_1}=\{(s,t) \in {\mathbb H} \mid {\mathbb R} Z_{\sigma_{(sH,tH)}}(v)=
 {\mathbb R}Z_{\sigma_{(sH,tH)}}(v_1) \}.
$$
head: environment

label: lem:wall
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:wall}
Let $W_{v_1}'$ be a connected component of $W_{v_1} \cap {\mathbb H}^0$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)]
$W_{v_1}$ is a semi-circle if $rd_1-r_1 d \ne 0$ and a vertical half line defined by $rs-d=0$ if $rd_1-r_1 d=0$.
\item[(2)]
For a point $(s_0,t_0) \in W_{v_1}'$,
we assume that there are $\sigma_{(s_0 H,t_0 H)}$-semistable 
objects $E_i$ $(i=1,2)$ such that $v(E_i)=v_i$ and
$\phi_{\sigma_{(s_0 H,t_0 H)}}(E_1)=\phi_{\sigma_{(s_0 H,t_0 H)}}(E_2)$.
Then $E_i$ are $\sigma_{(s H,t H)}$-semistable 
with $\phi_{\sigma_{(s H,t H)}}(E_1)=\phi_{\sigma_{(s H,t H)}}(E_2)$
for all $(s,t) \in W_{v_1}'$.
           
                                   
\item[(3)]
$W_{v_1}'$ is a wall in ${\mathbb H}^0$ 
if and only if $W_{v_1}'$ is a wall at a point.   
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Lemma \ref{lem:wall} (2) means that $\sigma_{(sH,tH)}$-semistability 
(resp. $\sigma_{(sH,tH)}$-stability) is independent 
along $W_{v_1}'$.

label: prop:stability-cond
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:stability-cond}
$$
U_\pm^\beta \subset {\mathbb H}^0.
$$
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Assume that $\gcd(p,q)=1$.
Let $U$ be a small neighborhood of $(\frac{q}{p},0) \in {\mathbb R}^2$. 
If $p \nmid (q^2 n+1)$, then
${\mathbb H}^0$ contains the half straight line defined by $ps-q=0$.
In this case, $U_+^\beta \cap U$ and $U_-^\beta \cap U$ belong to the same chamber
for $v=(0,0,1)$. 
On the other hand, if $p \mid (q^2 n+1)$, then
for the stability conditions $\sigma_+$ and $\sigma_-$
parameterized by $U_+^\beta \cap U$ and $U_-^\beta \cap U$ respectively,
$\sigma_+$ is far from $\sigma_-$ in the space of stability conditions.

label: prop:birational
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:birational}
Let $v=(r,dH,a)$ be a Mukai vector such that
$r \geq 0$, $d^\beta,a^\beta>0$ and $\langle v^2 \rangle \geq -2$. 
Then the following conditions are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)]
${\mathcal M}_H(v) \cap {\mathcal M}_{(sH,tH)}(v) \ne \emptyset$
for $(s,t) \in U_+^\beta(\nu)$ with $(0<\nu \ll 1)$.
\item[(2)]
\begin{enumerate}
\item
If $\langle v^2 \rangle>0$, then
$\langle v,v_1 \rangle \geq 0$ for $v_1 \in D_v^\beta$ with $\epsilon=1$ and
$\langle v,v_1 \rangle \geq 2$ for $v_1 \in D_v^\beta$ with $\epsilon=0$.
\item
If $\langle v^2 \rangle \leq 0$, then
$\langle v,v_1 \rangle \geq 0$ for $v_1 \in D_v^\beta$ with $\epsilon=1$. 
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The proof is similar to that of \cite[Prop. 3.6]{CNY}.
head: environment

title: Remark
head: environment

label: lem:stability
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:stability}
If  $t_1 \leq t \leq t_2$ and $(s,t_1) \in {\mathbb H}^0$, then 
$$
{\mathcal M}_{(sH,t_1 H)}(v) \cap {\mathcal M}_{(sH,t_2 H)}(v) \subset {\mathcal M}_{(sH,t H)}(v).
$$
In particular if ${\mathcal M}_{(sH,t_1 H)}(v) \cap {\mathcal M}_{(sH,t_2 H)}(v)  
\ne \emptyset$, then
${\mathcal M}_{(sH,t_1 H)}(v) \cap {\mathcal M}_{(sH,t H)}(v) \ne \emptyset$ 
for all $t_1 \leq t \leq t_2$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $E \in M_{(sH,t_1 H)}(v) \cap M_{(sH,t_2 H)}(v)$,
let $E_1$ be a subobject of $E$ in ${\mathcal A}_{(sH,tH)}$.
Since ${\mathcal A}_{(sH,tH)}$ is independent of the choice of $t$,
$E_1$ is a subobject of $E$ in ${\mathcal A}_{(sH,t'H)}$ for all 
$t_1 \leq t' \leq t_2$.
Then $\phi_{(sH,t_i H)}(E_1) \leq \phi_{(sH,t_i H)}(E)$ ($i=1,2$)
imply that $\phi_{(sH,tH)}(E_1) \leq \phi_{(sH,tH)}(E)$.
head: environment

label: lem:r_1<0
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:r_1<0}
Let $v=(r,dH,a)$ be a Mukai vector such that
$r,a^\beta \geq 0$, $d^\beta>0$ and $\langle v^2 \rangle \geq -2$.
Assume that $v_1=(r_1,d_1 H,a_1) \in D_v^\beta$ satisfies
$r_1 d^\beta-r d_1^\beta<0$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)]
Assume that $n \geq p^2$ and $\langle v^2 \rangle \geq 0$. 
Then $\langle v,v_1 \rangle \geq 2$ and the inequality is strict
unless $n=p^2$ and $r=a^\beta=0$.
\item[(2)]
Assume that $n \geq p(r+p)$ and $\langle v^2 \rangle = -2$. 
Then $\langle v,v_1 \rangle \geq 2$.
\end{enumerate}.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We note that $a_1^\beta d^\beta-a^\beta d_1^\beta<0$.
\begin{NB}
$v$ may not be primitive.
\end{NB}
If $r_1 \leq 0$, then $n (d_1^\beta)^2+\epsilon=r_1 a_1^\beta$ and $r_1 \ne 0$ imply
$r_1,a_1^\beta<0$. 
Hence
$$
\langle v,v_1 \rangle = 2nd^\beta d_1^\beta-r_1 a^\beta-r a_1^\beta 
\geq 2+a^\beta+r/p^2 \geq 2.
$$
\begin{NB}
The claim holds if $(d_1^\beta)^2 n \geq 1$.
If $(d_1^\beta)^2 n < 1$, then $d_1^\beta <1$.
For example, if $n=2$ and $p=2$, then $d_1^\beta=1/2$ and $(d_1^\beta)^2 n=1/2$.
\end{NB}
If the equality holds, then 
$n=p^2$ and $r=a^\beta=0$.
                                                        
                                                 
                              
\begin{NB}
If $d^\beta > p/2$, then
$d^\beta d_1^\beta >1/2$. Hence
$\langle v,v_1 \rangle>1$.
\end{NB}
 
If $r_1 >0$, then
$n (d_1^\beta)^2+\epsilon=r_1 a_1^\beta<r_1 a^\beta \frac{d_1^\beta}{d^\beta}$.
We first assume that $\langle v^2 \rangle \geq 0$.
By $r_1 d^\beta-r d_1^\beta \leq -1$,
we get $r>0$ and
$$
\frac{d_1^\beta}{r_1}n \geq \frac{d^\beta}{r} n +\frac{n}{r r_1}
\geq \frac{a^\beta}{d^\beta}+\frac{n}{r r_1}>\frac{a^\beta}{d^\beta}.
$$
Hence 
$$
r_1 d_1^\beta \frac{d_1^\beta}{r_1}n>r_1 a^\beta \frac{d_1^\beta}{d^\beta}>
n (d_1^\beta)^2+\epsilon \geq n(d_1^\beta)^2,
$$
which is a contradiction. Therefore (1) holds.
\begin{NB}
If $r_1>0$, then the assumption $n \geq p^2$ is not used. 
\end{NB}

Assume that $\langle v^2 \rangle=-2$. 
Then we also get $r>0$ and
$$
\frac{d_1^\beta}{r_1}n 
\geq \frac{a^\beta}{d^\beta}+\frac{1}{r} \left(\frac{n}{r_1}-\frac{1}{d^\beta} \right) =
\frac{a^\beta}{d^\beta}+\frac{1}{r} \left(\frac{n}{r_1}-\frac{p}{pd-qr} \right).
$$
Since $d_1^\beta \leq d^\beta$, we get $r_1<\frac{d^\beta_1}{d^\beta}r \leq r$.
Hence $n \geq pr \geq pr_1$.
Therefore 
$\frac{d_1^\beta}{r_1}n  \geq \frac{a^\beta}{d^\beta}$.
If $\epsilon=1$, then 
$$
r_1 d_1^\beta \frac{d_1^\beta}{r_1}n \geq
n (d_1^\beta)^2+1 > n(d_1^\beta)^2,
$$
which is a contradiction.
Therefore (2) holds.
head: environment

label: lem:r_1>0
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:r_1>0}
Let $v=(r,dH,a)$ be a Mukai vector such that
$r,a^\beta \geq 0$, $d^\beta>0$.
Assume that $v_1=(r_1,d_1 H,a_1) \in D_v^\beta$ satisfies
$r_1 d^\beta-r d_1^\beta>0$.
We set $k:=a_1^\beta d^\beta-a^\beta d_1^\beta>0$.
Then the following claims hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)]
\begin{equation}\label{eq:r_1>0}
\langle v,v_1 \rangle = \frac{1}{r_1 d_1}
\left(
(r_1 d^\beta-r d_1^\beta)(n(d_1^\beta)^2-\epsilon)-(2rd_1^\beta \epsilon -k r_1^2) \right).
\end{equation}
\item[(2)]
If $\langle v_1^2 \rangle=0$ and $n > p^2$, then
$\langle v,v_1 \rangle \geq 3$.
\item[(3)]
Assume that $p=1$ and $n=1$.
If $\langle v_1^2 \rangle=0$, then
$\langle v,v_1 \rangle \geq 3$ unless $v=(r,(r+1)H,r)$ and $v_1=(1,H,1)$.  
\end{enumerate}

title: Proof

label: lem:n>2p^2
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:n>2p^2}
Let $v_1=(r_1,d_1 H,a_1) \in D_v^\beta$ be a Mukai vector satisfying
$r_1 d^\beta-r d^\beta_1>0$ and $\langle v_1^2 \rangle=-2$. 
Assume that $n \geq 2p^2$ and $\langle v,v_1 \rangle<0$.
Then $r_1<r$ and $d_1^\beta<\frac{2r}{p^2}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By $n \geq 2p^2$ and $pd_1^\beta \in {\mathbb Z}$,
$(n-p^2)(d_1^\beta)^2\geq (p d_1^\beta)^2 \geq 1$.
Hence 
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
& (r_1 d-r d_1)(n (d_1^\beta)^2-1)-(2rd_1^\beta-kr_1^2)\\
\geq & n(d_1^\beta)^2-1-2r d_1^\beta+k r_1^2 \\
\geq & (pd_1^\beta)^2-2r d_1^\beta+k r_1^2 \\
=&
\left(pd_1^\beta-\tfrac{r}{p} \right)^2-\frac{r^2}{p^2}+k r_1^2
\end{split}
\end{equation}
If $r_1 \geq r$, then $kr_1^2 \geq \frac{r^2}{p^2}$.
If $d_1^\beta \geq \frac{2r}{p^2}$, then
$(pd_1^\beta)^2-2r d_1^\beta=d_1^\beta(p^2 d_1^\beta-2r) \geq 0$.
Therefore the claim holds.
head: environment

label: lem:stability-cond
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: prop:isom
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:isom}
Assume that $(s,t) \in {\mathcal C}$. Then
we have an isomorphism
$$
{\mathcal M}_{(sH,tH)}(v) \cong {\mathcal M}_{H'}(v')
$$
by sending $E \in {\mathcal M}_{(sH,tH)}(v)$ to
$\Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}}(E)^{\vee}$, where
$v'=\Phi_{X \to X'}^{\mathcal E}(v)^{\vee}$.
head: environment

label: prop:no-wall
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Proposition \ref{prop:stability-cond}, there is a segment 
$I(x) \in {\mathbb H}^0 (0 \leq x \leq 1)$ 
such that $I(0)=(0,t_\infty)$ is in the Gieseker chamber and
$I(1)=(s_1,t_1) \in {\mathcal C}$ and $0<s_1 \ll 1$. 
\begin{NB}
Let $(s(x) H,t(x) H)$ $(s(x) \geq 0)$ be a path in the space of 
geometric stability 
conditions connecting 
Gieseker chamber to ${\mathcal C}$.
\end{NB}
By Proposition \ref{prop:birational}, Lemma \ref{lem:r_1<0} and Lemma \ref{lem:r_1>0},
${\mathcal M}_H(r,dH,a) \cap {\mathcal M}_{(s_1 H,t_1 H)}(v) \ne \emptyset$
if and only if (2) holds.
Combining Proposition \ref{prop:isom},
we see that (1) is equivalent to (2).
head: environment

label: thm:n
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We note that $n>p^2$.
By Lemma \ref{lem:r_1<0} and Lemma \ref{lem:r_1>0},
it is sufficient to prove that
$\langle v,v_1 \rangle >0$ for $v_1=(r_1,d_1 H,a_1) \in D_v^\beta$
with $r_1>0$ and $\langle v_1^2 \rangle=-2$.
By $n \geq (2r+p)p$ and
\eqref{eq:r_1>0}, we see that
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
& n(d_1^\beta)^2-1-2r d_1^\beta+k r_1^2\\
\geq & (2r+p)p (d_1^\beta)^2-2r d_1^\beta-1+kr_1^2 \\
=& 2r(pd_1^\beta-1)d_1^\beta+(pd_1^\beta)^2-1+kr_1^2>0.\\
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Hence the condition in Proposition \ref{prop:no-wall} (2) holds.
Therefore our claim holds.
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md:
Let $v=(r,dH,a)$ be a Mukai vector satisfying \eqref{eq:cond-v}.
Assume that $n \geq 2p^2$ and $d-r\frac{q}{p} \geq 2r+2\frac{r^2}{p^2}$.
Then 
$\Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}}(E)^{\vee} \in {\mathcal M}_{H'}(v')$
for a general $E \in {\mathcal M}_H(v) \setminus Z$, where 
$v'=\Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}}(v)$ and $Z$ is a closed substack 
with $\dim Z \leq \dim {\mathcal M}_H(v)-2$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Assume that there is a totally semistable wall.
By Lemma \ref{lem:r_1<0} and Lemma \ref{lem:r_1>0},
it is defined by a Mukai verctor $v_1=(r_1,d_1 H,a_1) \in D_v^\beta$ satisfying
$r_1 d^\beta-r d^\beta_1>0$ and $\langle v_1^2 \rangle=-2$. 
We may assume that 
$r_1<r$ and $d_1^\beta<\frac{2r}{p^2}$ (Lemma \ref{lem:n>2p^2}).
Then
$r_1 d-r d_1 \geq d^\beta-rd_1^\beta \geq 2r$.
Hence
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
& (r_1 d-r d_1)(n (d_1^\beta)^2-1)-(2rd_1^\beta-kr_1^2)\\
\geq & 2r(n (d_1^\beta)^2-1-d_1^\beta)+kr_1^2 \\
\geq & 2r((p^2 (d_1^\beta)^2-1)+d_1^\beta (p^2 d_1^\beta-1))+kr_1^2>0.
\end{split}
\end{equation} 
Hence the condition in Proposition \ref{prop:no-wall} (2) holds, and hence
our claim holds.
head: environment

label: lem:aCM:remark
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:aCM:remark}
Let $v=(r,dH,a)$ be a Mukai vector such that
$r \geq 0,a^\beta \leq 0$, $d^\beta>0$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item
[(1)]
If $n \geq p^2$ and $p \nmid q^2 n+1$, then
$\langle v,v_1 \rangle>0$ for $v_1 \in D_v^\beta$.
\item
[(2)]
If $n>p^2$, then $\langle v,v_1 \rangle \geq 3$ if $\epsilon=0$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: eq:aCM:remark1
title: Proof
head: environment

label: thm:a<0
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:a<0}
Let $v=(r,dH,a)$ be a Mukai vector such that
$$
r \geq 0, \; pd-rq>0,\;
\langle v^2 \rangle \geq 0.
$$ 
Assume that $n > p^2$.
                        
If $\langle v,v_0 \rangle \geq 0$, then
$\Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}}(E)[1] \in {\mathcal M}_{H'}(v')$
for a general $E \in {\mathcal M}_H(v) \setminus Z$, where  
$v'=-\Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}}(v)$ and $Z$ is a closed substack of ${\mathcal M}_H(v)$
such that $\dim Z \leq \dim {\mathcal M}_H(v)-2$.
head: environment

label: thm:a<<0
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:a<<0}
For a fixed $r$ and $d$
with
$$
r>0,\; pd-qr>0,
$$
if 
$$
a^\beta \leq \min \left\{-\frac{p(pd-qr)}{r}, -p, -r,-2(pd-qr) \right\},
$$ 
then
$\Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}}(E)[1] \in {\mathcal M}_{H'}(v')$
for a general $E \in {\mathcal M}_H(v) \setminus Z$, where  
$v'=-\Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}}(v)$ and $Z$ is a closed substack of ${\mathcal M}_H(v)$
such that $\dim Z \leq \dim {\mathcal M}_H(v)-2$.
head: environment

label: eq:nkd
title: Proof
body_md:
(1)
Assume that $\langle v,v_1 \rangle \leq 2$ for $v_1 \in D_v^\beta$ with 
$\langle v_1^2 \rangle=0$.
By the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:aCM:remark} (2), we get
\begin{equation}\label{eq:nkd}
nk(r_1 d^\beta-rd_1^\beta) \leq 1.
\end{equation}
We shall prove that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:aCM:remark3}
a^\beta > \min \left\{-\frac{p(pd-qr)}{r}, -p \right\}.
\end{equation}

We first assume that $r_1 d^\beta-rd_1^\beta<0$ and
$k=a_1^\beta d^\beta-a^\beta d_1^\beta<0$.
Since $-kp^2 \in {\mathbb Z}_{>0}$, \eqref{eq:nkd} implies
$n(r_1 d^\beta-rd_1^\beta) \geq -p^2$.
By $r_1<0$, we have $d_1^\beta \leq \frac{p^2}{rn}$.
Since $r_1 a_1^\beta=(d_1^\beta)^2 n$,
$$
a^\beta>\frac{d^\beta}{d_1^\beta}a_1^\beta=
\frac{d^\beta d_1^\beta}{r_1}n>\frac{d^\beta p^2}{r_1 r}>\frac{d^\beta p^2}{-r}.
$$

We next assume that $r_1 d^\beta-rd_1^\beta>0$
and
$k=a_1^\beta d^\beta-a^\beta d_1^\beta>0$.
Then $kn \leq 1$. Hence
$$
a^\beta>\frac{a_1^\beta d^\beta-k}{d_1^\beta} \geq 
\frac{a_1^\beta d^\beta-1}{d_1^\beta}>-p.
$$

(2)
Assume that $\langle v,v_1 \rangle \leq 0$ for $v_1 \in D_v^\beta$ with 
$\langle v_1^2 \rangle=-2$.
We shall prove that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:aCM:remark4}
a^\beta > \min \left\{-r, -2(pd-qr) \right\}.
\end{equation}
 
If $r_1 d^\beta-rd_1^\beta>0$,
then by using the computation in \eqref{eq:aCM:remark1}, we see that  
$$
0 \geq \langle v,v_1 \rangle \geq -\frac{r}{r_1}-r_1 a^\beta.
$$
Hence $a^\beta>-r$.
 
If $r_1 d^\beta-rd_1^\beta<0$,
then the computation in \eqref{eq:aCM:remark2} implies that
$n(d_1^\beta)^2<1$.
Hence $-a_1^\beta=\frac{(d_1^\beta)^2n+1}{(-r_1)}<2$.
Therefore 
$$
a^\beta \geq \frac{d^\beta}{d_1^\beta}a_1^\beta > -2(pd-qr).
$$

By (1) and (2), our claim holds.
head: environment

label: rem:stable-kernel
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:stable-kernel} 
Let $\Phi_{X \to X}^{{\mathcal E}'}:{\bf D}(X) \to {\bf D}(X)$ be 
another Fourier-Mukai transform
which induces the same action on the Mukai lattice as $\Phi_{X \to X}^{{\mathcal E}}$.
Then ${\mathcal E}'_{|X \times \{ x \}}$ are simple complexes for all $x \in X$.
If they are simple sheaves for all $x \in X$, then
they are stable by \cite{Mukai:Tata}, and hence
we get ${\mathcal E'} \cong {\mathcal E}$.
Therefore ${\mathcal E}'$ is not a family of simple sheaves.
head: environment

label: lem:T(X)
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:T(X)}
Let $T(X)$ be the transcendental lattice of $X$.
Then the action of $D_X \circ \Phi_{X \to X}^{{\mathcal E}}$ on $T(X)$ is
trivial.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since
$-(pc+q^2 n)=-2q^2 n+1 \equiv 1 \mod 2n$, $\phi_A$ acts trivially on 
$$
H^*(X,{\mathbb Z})_{\operatorname{alg}}^{\vee}/H^*(X,{\mathbb Z})_{\operatorname{alg}}=\operatorname{NS}(X)^{\vee}/\operatorname{NS}(X) \cong
{\mathbb Z}/2n{\mathbb Z}.
$$
Since 
$$
T(X)^{\vee}/T(X) \cong \operatorname{NS}(X)^{\vee}/\operatorname{NS}(X)
$$
and the isometry group $O(T(X))$ consists of $\pm 1$ (\cite[Lem. 4.1]{Oguiso}), the claim holds.
head: environment

label: prop:bir-auto
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:bir-auto}
Let $v=(r,dH,a)$ $(r>0)$ be a Mukai vector such that 
$$
a=\frac{2npqd-(q^2 n-1)r}{p^2}.
$$
Then the following claims hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)]
$\phi_A(v)=v$.
\item[(2)]
If $n \geq 2rp+p^2$, then
$D_X \circ \Phi_{X \to X}^{{\mathcal E}}$ induces a birational involution of $M_H(v)$ which is non-symplectic.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(1) follows from \eqref{eq:phi}.

(2)
By Theorem \ref{thm:n}, $D_X \circ \Phi_{X \to X}^{{\mathcal E}}$ induces a birational map
$M_H(v) \cdots \to M_H(v)$.
Under the identification 
$$
v^\perp \cong H^2(M_H(v),{\mathbb Z}),
$$
the induced action on $v^\perp$ is the homomorphism $-D_X \circ \Phi_{X \to X}^{{\mathcal E}}$.
Hence it is a non-symplectic action.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
$v=e^{\frac{q}{p}H}(r,(d-\tfrac{q}{p}r)H,\tfrac{r}{p^2})$.
Hence $\langle v^2 \rangle/2=(d-\tfrac{q}{p}r)^2 n-\frac{r^2}{p^2}$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
For the existence of a birational involution, we do not need the assumption $n \geq 2rp+p^2$ by the work of
Bayer and Macri \cite{BM}.  Our assumption is used to specify the kernel of $\Phi_{X \to X}^{{\mathcal E}}$.
head: environment

label: ex:involution
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:involution}
Assume that $p^2 \mid(q^2 n-1)$. 
Let $r>0$ and $d$ be integers satisfying 
$p \mid 2d$. 
Then 
$$
a:=\frac{2npqd-(q^2 n-1)r}{p^2} \in {\mathbb Z}.
$$
For $v:=(r,dH,a)$, we can apply Proposition \ref{prop:bir-auto}.
In particular we have a non-symplectic birational automorphism
of $X^{[\ell+1]}$, where $\ell=\frac{q^2 n-1}{p^2}$.
head: environment

label: lem:reflection
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:reflection}
$$
\phi_A(u)=-(u+\langle u,v_0 \rangle v_0),\; u \in H^*(X,{\mathbb Z})_{\operatorname{alg}}.
$$
Thus $-\phi_A$ is the reflection by $v_0$.
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md:
Assume that $p \mid q^2 n+1$ and $E_0$ be a stable rigid vector bundle 
$v(E_0)=(p,qH,\frac{q^2 n+1}{p})$.
Let $v=(r,dH,a)$ be a Mukai vector such that
$$
r \geq 0,\; pd-qr>0,\; -\langle v,v_0 \rangle>0
$$
 and $\langle v^2 \rangle \geq -2$. 
Assume that $n \geq (2r+p)p$.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)]
$\operatorname{Ext}^1(E_0,E)=0$ for a general $E \in {\mathcal M}_H(v)$.
\item[(2)]
$\operatorname{coker}(E^{\vee} \to \operatorname{Hom}(E_0,E)^{\vee} \otimes E_0^{\vee} )$
is semistable for a general $E \in {\mathcal M}_H(v)$. 
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md:
Let $v=(r,dH,r)$ $(r,d>0)$ be a primitive Mukai vector. 
Assume that $\langle v_1,v \rangle=0$ for $v_1 \in D_v^\beta$ with
$\langle v_1^2 \rangle=-2$.
Then $v=(2,3H,2)$ and $v_1=(1,H,2),(2,H,1)$.
head: environment

label: eq:vv_1
title: Proof
body_md:
We note that $\gcd(r,d)=1$.
We assume that $\langle v_1,v \rangle=0$ for $v_1=(r_1,d_1 H,a_1) \in D_v^\beta$ with
$\langle v_1^2 \rangle=-2$.
Then 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:vv_1}
d_1^2+1=r_1 a_1,\;
2dd_1=r(a_1+r_1).
\end{equation}
By Lemma \ref{lem:r_1<0}, we get
\begin{equation}\label{eq:r_1a_1}
r_1>\frac{r d_1}{d},\; a_1 >\frac{r d_1}{d}.
\end{equation}

(1) We first treat the case where $r$ is odd.
Then we get 
\begin{equation}
d_1=kr,\; r_1+a_1=2kd\;\; (k \in {\mathbb Z}).
\end{equation}
                      
                                                            
If $r_1 \geq kd+1$, then by using \eqref{eq:r_1a_1}, we see that
$$
r_1 a_1\geq (kd+1)a_1=kda_1+a_1>krd_1+a_1=d_1^2+a_1
                                                         
$$
which contradicts \eqref{eq:vv_1}. 
Hence $r_1 \leq kd$. We also have $a_1 \leq kd$.
By $r_1+a_1=2kd$, $r_1=a_1=kd$.
Then $(kd)^2=(kr)^2+1$, and hence $r=0$ and $kd=1$, which is a contradiction.

(2) We next assume that $r$ is even.
Since $\gcd(r,d)=1$, $d$ is odd.
We set $r=2r'$.
Then 
\begin{equation}
d_1=kr',\; r_1+a_1=kd\; (k \in {\mathbb Z}). 
\end{equation}
By \eqref{eq:r_1a_1},
$r_1 \geq \frac{krr'+1}{d}$ and $a_1\geq \frac{krr'+1}{d}$.
Assume that $k$ is odd.
If $r_1 \geq \frac{kd+3}{2}$, then by using \eqref{eq:r_1a_1}, we see that
\begin{equation}
r_1 a_1\geq \left(\frac{kd+1}{2}+1 \right)a_1=
\left(\frac{kd+1}{2}\right)a_1+a_1>\frac{krd_1}{2}+a_1=d_1^2+a_1,
                                                      
           
\end{equation}
 
which contradicts \eqref{eq:vv_1}. 
Hence $r_1 \leq \frac{kd+1}{2}$. We also have $a_1 \leq \frac{kd+1}{2}$.
By $r_1+a_1=kd$, we see that
$\{r_1,a_1 \}=\{ \frac{kd-1}{2},\frac{kd+1}{2}\}$.
Hence we get 
$$
d_1^2+1=r_1 a_1=\frac{(kd)^2-1}{4}.
$$
                                                         
Then we see that $kd=3$ and $d_1=1$, and hence,
$k=r'=1$ and $d=3$. Therefore 
$v=(2,3H,2)$ and $v_1=(1,H,2),(2,H,1)$.

Assume that $k$ is even.
If $r_1 \geq \frac{kd+2}{2}$, then we see that
\begin{equation}
r_1 a_1\geq \left(\frac{kd}{2}+1 \right)a_1=
\frac{kd}{2}a_1+a_1>\frac{krd_1}{2}+a_1=d_1^2+a_1,
\end{equation}
 
which contradicts \eqref{eq:vv_1}. 
Hence $r_1 \leq \frac{kd}{2}$.
We also have $a_1 \leq \frac{kd}{2}$.
By $r_1+a_1= kd$, we see that $r_1=a_1=\frac{kd}{2}$. 
By solving the equation $\frac{(kd)^2}{4}=d_1^2+1$, 
we get $d_1=0$, which is a contradiction.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We set $l:=\gcd(n,r)$. Then
$r=r' l,n=n' l$ $(l \in {\mathbb Z})$.
We note that $r'$ is odd, $\gcd(r',dn')=1$, $n'>1$. 

We see that $d_1=r' k$, $r_1+a_1=2n' dk$.
If $r_1>\frac{ndd_1}{r}=n'dk$, then
$r_1 \geq n' dd_1+1$.
Then we get
$$
r_1 a_1 \geq n'dk a_1+a_1>nd_1^2+a_1. 
$$
Therefore $r_1 \leq n'dk$. similarly
we get $a_1 \leq n'dk$.
By $r_1+a_1=2n' dk$, $r_1=a_1=n'dk$.
Then we get $(n'dk)^2=d_1^2 n+1$, which contradicts $n'>1$.
Therefore there is no $v_1$.
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md:
Assume that $n > r$.
Then there is no totally semistable wall and codimension 1 wall
for $v=(r,dH,r)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Assume that $v_1 \in D_v^0$ with $\langle v,v_1 \rangle \leq 0$.
We note that
$$
\frac{ndd_1+1}{r}\frac{rd_1+1}{d}>nd_1^2+\frac{n}{r}d_1 \geq nd_1^2+1.
$$ 
Hence $r_1,a_1 \leq \frac{ndd_1}{r}$, which implies 
$\langle v,v_1 \rangle \geq 0$.
If the equality holds, then
$$
\left(\frac{ndd_1}{r} \right)^2=d_1^2 n+1.
$$
Then we get $\gcd(n,r)=n$, which contradicts to our assumption $n>r$.
Therefore $\langle v,v_1 \rangle>0$.
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md:
We set $v:=(r,(r+2)H,r)$ $(r \geq 5)$. 
Assume that $v_1=(r_1,d_1,a_1) \in D_v^\beta$ satisfies
$\langle v_1^2 \rangle=-2$ and $\langle v,v_1 \rangle \leq 0$.
Then $v_1=(1,H,2),(2,H,1)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma \ref{lem:r_1<0},
$r_1 d-r d_1>0$ and $a_1 d-a d_1>0$.
Since $d_1 \leq d=r+2$,
$$
r_1>\frac{r}{r+2}d_1=d_1-\frac{2d_1}{r+2} \geq d_1-2.
$$
Moreover $r_1>d_1-1$ if $d_1<\frac{r}{2}+1$.
Hence 
$r_1 \geq r-1$ and $r_1 \geq r$ if $d_1<\frac{r}{2}+1.$
We also have $a_1  \geq r-1$ and $a_1 \geq r$ if $d_1<\frac{r}{2}+1$.

Assume that $d_1 \geq 4$.
If $r_1 \geq d_1+2$, then 
$$
r_1 a_1 \geq (d_1+2)(d_1-1)>d_1^2+1=r_1 a_1.
$$
Hence $r_1 \leq d_1+1$.
We also get $a_1 \leq d_1+1$.
Then we see that $r_1 a_1 \ne d_1^2+1$.
Assume that $d_1 \leq 3$.
Then $d_1<\frac{r}{2}+1$, which implies
$r_1,a_1 \geq d_1$.
Then we see that $r_1 a_1 \ne d_1^2+1$ unless $v_1=(1,H,2), (2,H,1)$.
head: environment

label: lem:wall-L
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:wall-L}
For the Mukai vector $v=(r,dH,r)$ with $r>2(d-r)$,
we set $w_i:=v+\langle v,v(F_i) \rangle v(F_i)$.
Let $v_1=(r_1,d_1 H,a_1)$ $(d_1>0)$ be a $(-2)$-vector with
$$
\frac{a_1 d-rd_1}{r_1 d-rd_1}=\left(\frac{2d-r}{d-r}\right)^{(-1)^{i+1}}.
$$ 
Then $\langle w_i,v_1 \rangle>0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We only treat the case where $i=1$.
We note that $w_1=(2(d-r),3(d-r)H,4d-5r)$.
We set $L:=({\mathbb Q}v+{\mathbb Q}v(F_1)) \cap H^*(X,{\mathbb Z})_{\operatorname{alg}}$.
                                                                                     
Let $v_1=(r_1,d_1 H,a_1) \in L$ be a $(-2)$-vector such that
$d_1>0$.
Then $a_1=\frac{(2d-r)r_1-rd_1}{d-r}$.
If $r_1 \geq d_1$, then 
$$
a_1=\frac{(r_1-d_1)r}{d-r}+2r_1 \geq 2r_1 \geq 2d_1.
$$
Hence $d_1^2+1=r_1 a_1 \geq 2d_1^2$, which implies $v_1=(1,H,2)$.
In this case $\langle w_1,v_1 \rangle=3r-2d >0$.
If $r_1<d_1$, then
$\langle w_1,v_1 \rangle =(6(d-r)+2r)d_1-(8(d-r)+r)r_1>0$.
Therefore there is a $\sigma_{(0,t_0)}$-stable object $F$ with
$v(F)=w_1$, where $t_0=\sqrt{\frac{2d-r}{d-r}}$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
For $v=(r,(r+1)H,r)$, $(1,H,2)$ and $(2,H,1)$ still give totally semistable wall, but the birational automorphism 
of $M_H(v)$
is slightly different. In this case, $\langle v,(1,H,1) \rangle=0$ and
defines a wall for the movable cone. So
$D_X \circ \Phi_{X \to X}^{{\mathcal E}} \circ \Psi$ induces a birational map 
acting trivially on the movable cone of $M_H(v)$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Assume that $v=(r,(r+3)H,r)$. Then a similar claim holds for $r \geq 7$.
Thus $\langle v,v_1 \rangle \leq 0$ iff $v_1=(1,H,2),(2,H,1)$ and
they define totally semistable walls.
In particular \eqref{eq:Psi} holds.
head: environment

label: eq:varphi
title: Proposition
body_md:
Assume that $t \geq p_1 s(p_1 s+2)$ and $s \ne 1$.
For a general homomorphism
 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:varphi}
\varphi:E_0 \to \oplus_{i=1}^{\ell+1} {\mathcal E}_{|X \times \{ x_i' \}},
\end{equation}
 
one of the following holds:
\begin{enumerate}
\item
$\varphi^{\vee}$ is injective and $\operatorname{coker} \varphi^{\vee} \in {\mathcal M}_H(u_1'-\ell u_0')$. 
Moreover a general $F \in {\mathcal M}_H(u_1'-\ell u_0')$ is given in this way, where 
$\varphi^{\vee}$ is the dual of $\varphi$ and
$u_i'=D_X(u_i)$. 
\item
$\varphi$ is injective and $\operatorname{coker} \varphi \in {\mathcal M}_H(\ell u_0-u_1)$.
Moreover a general $F \in {\mathcal M}_H(\ell u_0-u_1)$ is given in this way. 
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $s,t>1$, ${\mathcal E}$ is a family of $\mu$-stable vector bundles on $X$.
By \cite{Y:Stability} or \cite{FM-duality},
${\mathcal E}$ is regarded as a universal family of $\mu$-stable vector bundles on $X'$. 
Replacing ${\mathcal E}$ if necessary, we may assume that
$\Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}}(u_1)=(1,0,0)$.
By $t \geq p_1 s(p_1 s+2)$, Theorem \ref{thm:n} implies
$\Phi_{X' \to X}^{{\mathcal E}}({\mathcal O}_{X'})$ is a stable sheaf with the Mukai vector
$u_0+u_1$.
Hence $E_0= \Phi_{X' \to X}^{{\mathcal E}}({\mathcal O}_{X'})$.
Then 
the complex \eqref{eq:varphi} is the Fourier-Mukai transform
$\Phi_{X' \to X}^{{\mathcal E}}$
of the complex
$$
{\mathcal O}_{X'} \to {\mathcal O}_Z,
$$ 
where $Z=\{x_1',x_2',...,x_{\ell+1}' \}$.
\begin{NB}
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
\operatorname{Hom}(E_0,{\mathcal E}_{|X \times \{ x' \}})=& {\mathbb C}\\
\operatorname{Ext}^1(E_0,{\mathcal E}_{|X \times \{ x' \}})=&0\\
\operatorname{Ext}^2(E_0,{\mathcal E}_{|X \times \{ x' \}})=&0
\end{split}
\end{equation}
for all $x' \in X'$.
\end{NB} 
                                                                                          
Since $t \geq p_1 s(p_1 s+2)$, we can apply Theorem \ref{thm:n} and theorem \ref{thm:a<0}.
Thus $\Phi_{X' \to X}^{{\mathcal E}}(I_Z)^{\vee}$ is a stable sheaf for a general $I_Z$ if 
$p_2^2 t-\ell p_1^2 s \geq 0$ and
$\Phi_{X' \to X}^{{\mathcal E}}(I_Z)[1]$ is a stable sheaf for a general $I_Z$
if $p_2^2 t-\ell p_1^2 s<0$.
Therefore our claim holds.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Under the assumption $\Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}^{\vee}}(E_0)[2]={\mathcal O}_{X'}$,
if $\ell$ is sufficiently large, then Theorem \ref{thm:a<<0} implies
$\operatorname{coker} \varphi$ is stable for a general $\varphi$. 
For example, assume that $p_1=1$. Then $h^1({\mathcal E}_{|\{ x \} \times X'})=0$
for a general $x \in X$
(see \cite[Thm. 1.1 (2)]{CNY}). Then $\Phi_{X' \to X}^{{\mathcal E}}({\mathcal O}_{X'})^{\vee}$ is a sheaf, and hence
a rigid stable bundle by \cite{Mukai:Tata}.
Hence $\Phi_{X' \to X}^{{\mathcal E}}({\mathcal O}_{X'})=E_0$.
head: environment

label: thm:abel
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:abel}
Let $v=(r,dH,a)$ be a Mukai vector such that
$$
r \geq 0, \; pd-rq>0,\;
\langle v^2 \rangle \geq 0.
$$ 
Assume that $n \geq p^2$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)] 
If $\langle v,v_0 \rangle<0$, then
$D_{X'} \circ \Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}}(E) \in {\mathcal M}_{H'}(v')$
for a general $E \in {\mathcal M}_H(v) \setminus Z$, where  
$v'=D_{X'} \circ \Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}}(v)$ and $Z$ is a closed substack of ${\mathcal M}_H(v)$. 
Moreover if $n >p^2$, then $\dim Z \leq \dim {\mathcal M}_H(v)-2$
\item[(2)]
If $\langle v,v_0 \rangle \geq 0$, then
$\Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}}(E)[1] \in {\mathcal M}_{H'}(v'')$
for a general $E \in {\mathcal M}_H(v) \setminus Z$, where  
$v''=-\Phi_{X \to X'}^{{\mathcal E}}(v)$ and $Z$ is a closed substack of ${\mathcal M}_H(v)$. 
Moreover $\dim Z \leq \dim {\mathcal M}_H(v)-2$
                         
                                   
                              
                  
      
                                                   
      
                      
                             
                
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: prop:p>s,t
title: Proposition
head: environment

label: eq:v
title: Proof
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md:
\begin{enumerate}
\item
Assume that $n$ is a power of a prime.
If $n \geq p$, then there is no totally semistable wall on $s=\frac{q}{p}$.
\item
Assume that $p=2$.
Then there is no totally semistable wall on $s=\frac{q}{p}$ if $n \geq 2$.
\item
Assume that $p=3$.
Then there is no totally semistable wall on $s=\frac{q}{p}$
if $n \geq 3$.
\item
Assume that $p \geq 3$.
Then
there is no totally semistable wall on $s=\frac{q}{p}$
if $n>(p-1)(p-2)$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $s,t$ be positive integers such that $n=st$,
$\gcd(s,t)=1$ and $s,t <p$. We may assume that $s>t$.
If $n$ is a power of a prime, then $p>s=n$.
If $p=2,3$, then
$s=t=1$ or $p=3$ and $(s,t)=(1,2)$.
Hence $n<p$.
Assume that $p \geq 3$. 
By $s \leq p-1$ and $t \leq p-2$, we get $n \leq (p-1)(p-2)$.
Therefore our claims follow from Proposition \ref{prop:p>s,t}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
\begin{enumerate}
\item
If $n<p$, then there is a totally semistable wall on $s=\frac{q}{p}$.
We take $\beta=-\frac{1}{p}$.
Then
$v_1=(n,-H,1)$ defines a totally semistable wall for $v=(n\ell,-\ell H,\ell)$.
\item
If $n$ is not a power of prime, then
there is a totally semistable wall on $s=\frac{q}{p}$
even if $n \geq p$ in general.

Indeed for 
$n=6$, we set $v=\ell (2,H,3)-(3,2H,8)$.
Then $v_1=(2,H,3)$ defines a totally semistable wall on $s=\frac{3}{5}$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
For the totally semistable wall in the proof of Proposition \ref{prop:p>s,t},
$p_1,p_2<p$.
By $q_2=\frac{p_2 q_1 t+1}{p_1 s}$ and \eqref{eq:pq},
the choice of $q_1,q_2$ is finite.
Therefore there are finitely many choices of $v=(r,dH,a)$ with a totally semistable wall on $s=\frac{q}{p}$,
 if we fixed $r$ or $\langle v^2 \rangle$.
head: environment

title: Example
body_md:
Assume that $p=2$ and $n=1$.
If there is a totally semistable wall, then
$$
s=t=p_1=p_2=p_1 q_2 s-p_2 q_1 t=p_1 qs-pq_1=q_2 p-p_1 q_2 s=1.
$$
Hence $q=2q_1+1$ and
$q_2=q_1+1$.
Then
$$
v=(\ell-1,-H,-1)e^{q_1 H}, (\ell-1,\ell H,\ell)e^{q_1 H},\;(\ell>1)
$$
or $v=(0,H,1)e^{q_1 H}$.
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md:
If $|d-\frac{q}{p}r| \geq p+\frac{r}{n}$, then 
there is no totally semistable wall on $s=\frac{q}{p}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md:
Let $v=(r,dH,a)$ be a Mukai vector such that $r>0$ and 
$\langle v^2 \rangle=2\ell$.
Assume that $\ell \geq p^2+r$. Then there is no totally semistable wall on $s=\frac{q}{p}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Assume that there is a totally semistable wall on $s=\frac{q}{p}$.
Then $r=\pm(\ell_1 p_1^2 s-\ell_2 p_2^2 t)$.

If $r=\ell_1 p_1^2 s-\ell_2 p_2^2 t$, then
$\ell p_1^2 s-p_2^2 t \geq \ell-p_2^2>r$ and
$p_1^2 s- \ell p_2^2 t < p^2-\ell \leq -r$, which contradicts 
our assumption $\ell_1 p_1^2 s-\ell_2 p_2^2 t = r$.

If $r=\ell_2 p_2^2 t-\ell_1 p_1^2 s$, then
$\ell p_2^2 t-p_1^2 s \geq \ell-p_1^2>r$ and
$p_2^2 t- \ell p_1^2 s < p^2-\ell \leq -r$,
which congtradicts our assumption
$r=\ell_2 p_2^2 t-\ell_1 p_1^2 s$.

Therefore our claim holds.
head: environment
